name: Foreigner's Permanent Residence Permit -- Talent and Spouse tracks (Five-Star Card)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires employment at a qualifying institution -- a State Council department or provincial-government-affiliated body, or a high-and-new-technology enterprise, encouraged-category foreign-invested enterprise, advanced-technology foreign-invested enterprise, or export-oriented foreign-invested enterprise.
requirements.fix_path: Secure employment at a qualifying institution or enterprise category.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires holding a senior management or senior technical role at the qualifying institution, or meeting an equivalent high-level-talent standard.
requirements.fix_path: Document seniority in a senior management or senior technical capacity.

requirement_groups.name: PhD holder, or 4 years in a nationally-designated key development zone

requirements.blocker_text: For overseas Chinese specifically (huaren), a doctoral degree working in China, or 4 continuous years of work in a nationally-designated key-development region, is sufficient to apply -- a materially lower bar than the general high-level-talent track, reflecting a 2019 National Immigration Administration policy of 12 immigration facilitation measures aimed at overseas Chinese specifically.
requirements.fix_path: Complete a PhD and secure Chinese employment, or accrue 4 continuous years of work in a designated key-development zone.

requirement_groups.name: Spouse of a Chinese citizen or permanent resident

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a marriage to a Chinese citizen, or to a foreigner who already holds Chinese permanent residence, that has lasted 5 or more years, combined with 5 years of physical residence in China at 9 or more months per year, and stable living conditions.
requirements.fix_path: Maintain the marriage and required physical presence in China until both 5-year thresholds are met.

evidence_required.document: Employment or role documentation matching the applicable track's institution/seniority requirements
Marriage certificate and 5 years of residence records (spouse track)
Health certificate and overseas criminal-record certificate

outcome.duration_length: indefinite (card itself valid 10 years for adults, 5 for minors, renewed as a card only)

sources.title: National Immigration Administration (nia.gov.cn) -- 外国人在中国永久居留审批管理办法 (Administrative Measures for the Approval of Foreigners' Permanent Residence in China)

Nantong Municipal Foreign Affairs Office (a local government body, .gov.cn domain) -- official FAQ for overseas Chinese applying for permanent residence, citing the National Immigration Administration's 2019 package of 12 immigration facilitation measures and its PhD/4-year-key-zone provision specifically

notes: Three genuinely distinct qualifying groups, correctly modeled as OR-logic per this schema's core design decision: high-level talent employed at a qualifying institution (the general professional track, open to any nationality), a specifically overseas-Chinese-targeted PhD/key-zone track introduced via a 2019 National Immigration Administration policy package (12 immigration facilitation measures), and the spouse-of-citizen-or-PR track (5 years marriage plus 5 years' 9-months/year residence). The overseas-Chinese PhD/key-zone track is a genuine structural finding worth flagging clearly: it is materially easier than the general high-level-talent track (no requirement to work at a specific institution category, no explicit seniority test) but is explicitly restricted to huaren (foreign nationals of Chinese descent) rather than being open to all applicants -- a real, confirmed instance of ancestry functioning as a qualifying-path accelerant within China's permanent-residence system specifically, even though (per cn_chinese_descent_5yr_visa's notes) it doesn't create any general ancestry-based visa or automatic status outside this narrow context. education_level's 'phd' value is used as an imperfect proxy for the full compound test (PhD-and-employed-in-China, OR 4-years-in-a-key-zone) since the schema's closed attribute list has no clean single field for this OR-within-an-OR structure -- flagged honestly as a schema-fit simplification rather than silently collapsed into a single clean-looking requirement, consistent with how similar imperfect fits were handled for Poland's repatriation route and Saudi Arabia's real-estate-zone exclusion. Same top-level finding applies as on cn_green_card_investor: none of these tracks lead to or accelerate Chinese citizenship, which requires a wholly separate application under Nationality Law Article 7 (see cn_naturalisation) -- China's Green Card and its citizenship track are more sharply separated from each other than in almost any other country in this dataset.
